_about: Decisions for the kit's printed-year gate (kit/tools/livingyears.py, run by npm run check:living --years). Each entry removes its text from what the gate reads and carries its reason. Counts and slugs only: no living person's name or year belongs here. The older registry, data/living-year-allow.tsv, belongs to tools/livingyears.py and is read as it stands.

allow.why: A typing slip in the tree, not a birth: this archive's own correction (corrections.json) records that the man's parents died in 1888 and 1891 and that his birth entry cites a register that ends in 1884. His year is corrected to 1862 on his page (data/tree-corrections.tsv, 26 October 2026) and he is a deceased person again; this is the correction quoting the tree's year (slug georgius-prpic).

The same typing slip, quoted by the archive's own 'cannot be true' correction on his father's page (slug domianus-perpic), and by the corrections list of the tree's wrong dates. Not a living person's birth; see the first entry.

The same typing slip, quoted unaccented in the archive's own list of disputed dates (corrections.json) and in What Cannot Be True, which reports what the tree says. Not a living person's birth; see the first entry.
The same typing slip, as What Cannot Be True prints it where the name is a link to his page (the autolinker links him now he has died again). Not a living person's birth; see the first entry.
The same typing slip, as the search index holds What Cannot Be True's list, folded to lower case. Not a living person's birth; see the first entry.
The same correction's argument that Austria-Hungary ceased to exist in 1918, so a birth there in 1962 is impossible. A year in an argument, not a birth.
